normative_conclusion: Actual OS process replacement requires a changed runtime boot and a changed host-visible (PID, proc-stat starttime) identity for each Host and native process. Cross-lifetime PID-namespace inode inequality is not required: the namespace identifier can be recycled after retirement. The changed predicate implements that distinction without weakening the separate private-namespace or old-process-retirement checks.

reviewed_guards.detail: Exact receipt keys, canonical UUID string, exact list shape, positive exact integers with bool denied, distinct Host/native PIDs, and equal Host/native pidns within each row remain. Each role's PID/starttime pair must change and boot must change. A changed namespace cannot conceal the same PID/starttime incarnation. Recycled namespace with new incarnations is accepted.

Await old retirement before start_host, launch READY and renew, collect actual replacement process receipt, compare identity and boot, drain replacement, close IPC, then census and offline historical readers. The 30-line delta does not change these call sites.

Exact-owned inspection; native drain; IPC close; Docker Stop and readback; Running false and exact-int ExitCode zero; endpoint absence; absence of every recorded old PID/starttime identity; lock reacquisition; uncertainty and cleanup-failure latches must be clear. No changed predicate bypasses retirement.

Full exact-owned containment inspection precedes docker start. HostConfig.PidMode must remain empty/private, the stock command and UID/config guards remain, Host NSpid must end in 1, exact module command and stable proc-stat starttime are measured, native is the sole observed Host child, live installed-byte inventory is verified, and same pidns within each receipt is retained. No new requirement for cross-lifetime inode uniqueness is justified.
